children: China is signaling that some of its biggest technology companies may be permitted to buy Nvidia’s
newly released RTX Pro 5500 chips, potentially opening another channel for the U.S. chipmaker in the strategically important Chinese market.
Chinese regulators have asked companies including Alibaba

) about their plans to purchase the high-end graphics processors, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has sought details including expected order volumes and how the chips would be used.
According to the report, officials have indicated to some companies that the purchases are likely to receive approval.
Any easing of Beijing’s restrictions could be positive for Nvidia

by restoring access to Chinese customers at a time when U.S. export controls have sharply complicated its business in the country. China remains an important market for advanced computing hardware, while Alibaba

) and other technology companies are spending heavily to build AI infrastructure. The size of the potential opportunity will depend on how broadly China approves purchases and whether U.S. export rules permit Nvidia to supply the chips.
has been caught between restrictions imposed by Washington and Beijing as the two countries compete over artificial intelligence and advanced semiconductor technology.
The U.S. government recently relaxed restrictions on certain Nvidia products destined for China. However, shipments have largely involved older-generation chips and relatively small volumes.

The RTX Pro 5500 was introduced this month. Beijing’s apparent willingness to consider purchases suggests Nvidia could regain some Chinese sales even as both governments continue to place limits on access to advanced computing technology.

title: China may allow Alibaba, ByteDance to buy Nvidia’s new RTX Pro 5500 chips
